text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to split the console rendering path into a lightweight view-controller that composes panels and a streaming tile executor that does heavy aggregation. Goals: reduce tail latency for small interactive panels, enable incremental updates, and decouple RBAC evaluation for performance. Sketch below, want quick takes.

kenji: +1 on separation. main worry is correctness/ordering for panels that rely on consistent snapshots (e.g., heatmaps). streaming tiles are eventual; panels need a way to indicate staleness. :thinking_face:

maria: Right — plan is to support two read modes per panel: `blocking_fetch` (current behavior) and `streaming_inc_updates` (new opt-in). streaming mode shows a small "stale" badge until all required tiles arrive. Paid customers can keep blocking mode.

samir: On RBAC: two options we discussed earlier — pushdown auth into the query/tile executor vs. post-filter in view-controller. Pushdown reduces IO but couples tile executor to policy service. Post-filter keeps executor simple but cache effectiveness suffers (per-principal cache explosion).

lucy: Cache explosion is real. If we post-filter, every cache key needs a principal salt which multiplies entries. Could be 10–100x depending on org cardinality. That will kill memory & read cache hit rate.

maria: Agreed. Middle-ground: keep pushdown for common tenant-level policies (fast path) and do post-filtering for rare edge policies (complex ACL expressions). Also introduce a short-lived per-principal policy cache with a `policy_version` token on tile responses so view-controller can cheaply detect invalidation.

kenji: Implementation/rollout note: we should avoid a single big-bang cutover. propose: (1) implement streaming read API that mirrors existing tile API but marks `policy_version`, (2) add view-controller behind feature flag for a small set of orgs, (3) canary on 10% dashboards, allow fallback to monolith on error. Need per-panel telemetry: tokens consumed, tile latency, and `policy_version` mismatch rate.

samir: Migration steps I suggest: 1) Add `GET /v1/tiles/stream?panel_id=...` that returns chunked JSON events; 2) Tile executor returns `policy_version`; 3) View-controller performs RBAC pushdown if it has a valid cached `policy_version` else requests evaluation from auth service (async) and can block or serve stale depending on panel mode.

maria: Example panel config (proto-ish):
```
panel_config: {
  id: "org-123.cost-trend",
  mode: "streaming_inc_updates",
  consistency: "eventual_with_stale_indicator",
  cache_ttl: "30s",
  fallback: "blocking_fetch"
}
```

lucy: A few more cache design notes: use a two-tier key: `tenant:projection:panel_params` as the shared primary key, and then `tenant:principal:projection:panel_params` for salted entries only when the policy requires per-principal filtering. Keep salted entries TTL short (30s). Use approximate counting to detect when salted layer is growing and trigger a policy to prefer pushdown for that projection.

kenji: Telemetry: add `view_controller.panel.latency`, `tile_executor.tile.latency`, `view_controller.policy_mismatch`, `view_controller.cache_hit.salted` counters. We'll need dashboards to watch memory and cache churn during canary.

samir: For Dedicated/Private customers we must preserve KMS/HSM and allow on-prem policy evaluation. Add an `auth_capabilities` header in the tile API that indicates which auth modes are available (e.g., `auth_capabilities: [pushdown, remote-eval]`). View-controller should fall back to remote-eval for customers that disable pushdown.

maria: Good call. Also add a tiny compatibility shim in the monolith: if view-controller sees `500` from tile executor, it should `GET /v1/panels/:id/render` on the monolith and merge that snapshot as fallback. That gives safe rollback.

kenji: Rollout checklist (high-level):
- RFC + design doc posted (maria)
- telemetry + new metrics (kenji)
- cache key & policy_version spec (lucy)
- streaming API prototype (samir)
- beta opt-in UI toggle in Console (product)
- canary rollout (deploy-bot)

maria: Action items: @kenji add telemetry dashboard and alerts, @lucy write cache key spec + eviction policy, @samir prototype streaming API and `policy_version` header, I'll draft the RFC with cutover checklist.

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary window: 2025-02-03T09:00:00Z -> 2025-02-03T12:00:00Z. Example rollout command for canary (ops):
```
kubectl -n console rollout restart deployment/view-controller --record
# follow up with: kubectl set env deployment/view-controller FEATURE_VIEW_CONTROLLER=true --record
```

lucy: Minor concern — ensure the stale badge UX is explicit for security-sensitive dashboards (don't show partial billing numbers without clear indicator). We'll pair with product on messaging.

maria: Agreed. UX will show a lock icon + timestamp of last full snapshot. We'll make blocking mode the default for billing/alert panels.

kenji: Sounds like a solid plan. If everyone OK I'll merge a short RFC draft by EOD and start telemetry PRs tomorrow. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks all — will share draft shortly.
